name: Hotel des Indes (The Hague)
scope: Historic hotel exterior at Lange Voorhout, rounded entrance, ochre facades and roofline; exclude interior rotunda reconstruction.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

review.method: Qualla first, then exact rights-holder CC0 negatives and native model/map/roof comparison at approximate medium-fi scope.
review.notes: Two exact1971HansPeters/Anefo negatives, each explicitly releasedCC0 by its rights holder NationaalArchief, establish the surviving four-storey facade, seven flat axes and rounded corner, central three-bay pediment, rusticated base, balcony and curved entrance hierarchy. These identifying forms match the current model. The model retains the native mapped envelope and original public AHN4roof-height controls (about28.55mNAP versus2.65mstreet), not a roof reconstructed from the1971photo. Later mansard shape/dormers, hidden roofs/courts and modern glazed vestibule remain conservative medium-fi approximations; the archival photographs do not certify those additions. Yellow repaint is supported by Qualla narrative, not inferred from monochrome pixels. Fine sculpture, canopy ironwork and exact restoration are simplified. Accepted at approximate exterior scope; no historic1971restoration or complete current photographic coverage is claimed.

The palace underwent a four-year refurbishment and was opened on May 1, 1881. It got the current name inspired by the then famous Hotel des Indes in Batavia in the hope of attracting travelers from the Dutch East Indies.

Madurodam is a miniature city located in Scheveningen, The Hague, in the Netherlands. It is a model of a Dutch town on a 1:25 scale, composed of typical Dutch buildings and landmarks, as are found at various locations in the country. This major Dutch tourist attraction was built in 1952 and has been visited by tens of millions of visitors ever since.

De Prinsenhof. Negen aan elkaar geschakelde torens langs de Prinses Beatrixlaan. Het complex bevat 60.000 m2 kantoorruimte, een horecaplein, 1.000 parkeerplaatsen, een viersterren-hotel, 2.000 m2 fitness, winkels, kinderopvang en 207 luxe huurappartementen. Het complex ligt rechts van de Utrechtsebaan (A12 Utrecht-Den Haag). Opgeleverd in 2006.
